units.name: 121 Code as Rules
units.passage: We tend to regard dress codes as limits placed on our personal liberty, but they may actually rescue us from the constant scrutiny that surrounds what we wear. Paradoxically, today's casual and quirky culture, which celebrates individuality, can demand conformity just as strictly as a company with the strictest rules about attire. Such unspoken expectations are often harder to satisfy than any official code. A written dress code asks only that we follow it; when no such code exists, however, people are left drifting, obliged to find their way among countless unclear, unstated, or disputed norms. The more choices we are given, the heavier the burden of living up to those norms becomes, right down to the tiniest details of an outfit designed to look effortless. In short, we are at liberty to put on whatever we like, yet we remain tied to what others expect of us. According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the amount of clothing Americans throw away has risen by 750 percent since 1960, which happens to be around the time when much of American society started giving up clear shared rules about dress. This striking figure may point to endless unsuccessful attempts to find the right thing to wear in a world that offers no rules but plenty of judgment.

items.exp: 정해진 규정이 없으면 불분명한 기준을 스스로 찾아야 하고, 선택의 폭이 넓어질수록 부담이 커진다고 했어요. 결국 원하는 옷을 입을 자유가 있어도 타인의 기대에 묶인다는 것이 요지예요.

units.name: 122 Negotiation Tactics
units.passage: Many of us have turned niceness into a tool for keeping social life running smoothly: we stay polite and dodge disagreement so that each day passes with as little friction as possible. Yet this kind of niceness is frequently a trick. Once niceness becomes mere grease for social machinery, it loses its meaning, and a gesture such as a strained smile ends up signaling a silent wish to get away rather than genuine goodwill. For a skilled negotiator, this is fatal, because success depends on uncovering the hidden motives and limitations of the people across the table. To draw out such information, you must make the other side feel safe and in charge. Strange as it may seem, the way to do this is to invite the other party to say no, to mark out their own limits clearly, and to clarify what they want by stating what they reject. For this reason, I suggest you think of this approach as the opposite of the niceness trick. It is not opposite because it is rude; it is opposite because it is honest. Getting a counterpart to say "No" breaks down the hollow pretense of a vague "Yes" and exposes what really matters in the deal.

units.name: 123 Why People Click
units.passage: Certain narrative documentaries now borrow the storytelling devices of fiction, plot twists included, and critics warn that this may be a step too far. When filmmakers hold back facts merely so that a surprising twist can entertain the audience, they overshadow the very qualities for which documentaries have traditionally been valued. For decades, the documentary has defined itself in contrast to fictional cinema, earning respect for its commitment to truth, its ability to depict reality, and the knowledge it offers. People who still hold this view are the most likely to believe that loading a documentary with too many fictional techniques eventually weakens those strengths. Their objection usually expresses a wider concern about the role documentaries play today. If films mislead viewers simply to tell a more dramatic tale or to deliver "emotional punches," audiences may stop treating them as a reliable means of learning about and understanding the actual world. Worse still, this trend emerges in an era already marked by post-truth politics, alternative facts, and fake news. Seen in this light, such documentaries risk leading us deeper into the fog, making it even harder to tell what is real from what is invented.

choices: 다큐멘터리의 재미는 극적인 반전에서 나온다.

revealing hidden truths about the real world

units.name: 124 Personal Data Protection
units.passage: Online privacy policies are built on a myth: the idea that people will negotiate over their privacy or walk away from arrangements they find too intrusive. Yet how is someone applying for a job online supposed to weigh privacy concerns? The situation is hardly better anywhere else. A website's terms of service are not so much privacy policies as contracts in which users hand their rights over to the site's owner. Read the fine print closely and you will discover that it shields companies while offering almost nothing to the users who automatically click "I agree." The latest tactic of corporations is a clause allowing them to revise the agreement on their own, without even informing users. The arrangement looks like a market transaction, but underneath it resembles feudalism; everyone knows which side holds the power. Some propose that consumers should demonstrate they have understood the terms before accepting them, but when did any consumer last succeed in renegotiating a contract? Changing the terms set by a giant intermediary such as Facebook or Google lies far beyond what most users could hope to achieve. For this reason, regulators must require openness about the enormous amount of data being gathered. We must not let the rulers of online platforms exercise unlimited and hidden control over our information.

units.name: 125 Rights in Tension
units.passage: Researchers who examine the right to speak one's native tongue tend to treat language chiefly as an element of identity rather than as a means of communication. Their perspective draws attention to the lives of minority groups in countries where many languages are spoken and to those groups' need to voice their distinctive cultures and identities. These scholars rarely frame the issue as a question of how limited resources should be shared out among language communities. What they fail to acknowledge, however, is that resources are never unlimited, so any effort to cater to linguistic diversity in the marketplace must compete with attempts to meet other equally valid needs. Consider the money a school district spends on hiring teachers who can instruct in several languages: that same money could have been used to support the learning needs of students with disabilities. International human rights agreements and academic writing tend to cloud this matter of cost, since they present diversity as a precious cultural treasure and thereby hide the sacrifices that such choices demand. In reality, the issue calls for a balanced debate, one that weighs diversity and cultural identity alongside social responsibility and the costs that come with it.

units.name: 126 City Growth
units.passage: Paris stands as a carefully ordered whole, celebrated for grand monuments that can be seen clearly because no nearby structures block the view. Rather than growing gradually denser over time like most cities, it was shaped in the mid-to-late nineteenth century according to one unified plan, carried out by a master builder backed by imperial authority. Shakespeare famously suggested that a city is nothing but its people, and he was right, yet people require buildings to live in. A city must expand either upward or outward; when it stops doing so, residents lose the closeness to jobs, schools, and one another that urban life promises. Paradoxically, keeping a city intact may mean giving up part of it. In Paris, the modern urge to preserve everything has transformed a once affordable city into an exclusive boutique for the rich. Generations of artists spent their hard, formative early years in Paris, but how many struggling painters or writers could manage the rent in the city center now? Cities grow vertically or horizontally, and excessive preservation blocks the construction of better housing for the people who live there. Protecting the finest pieces of our urban heritage certainly has great worth, but when history turns into a straitjacket, a city sacrifices one of its most valuable strengths: its capacity to grow.

units.name: 127 Social Movements
units.passage: Every one of us arrives in a world already shaped by history, a world governed by certain customs and beliefs. Because these arrangements surround us from birth, we tend to accept them as natural and permanent, rarely asking whether they could be otherwise. In this sense, the dead keep a firm hold on the living: the habits of earlier generations quietly steer us toward one predictable path. The study of history weakens that hold. By showing how earlier societies were organized in very different ways, it uncovers alternatives that people in the past could never have pictured. History does not dictate which road we ought to take, yet it widens the range of roads we are able to see. That is why movements that hope to transform society frequently start by retelling the past, so that people can envision a different tomorrow. Whether the goal is to persuade laborers to strike or to encourage marginalized groups to claim their rights, the revised story carries the same message: the way things are today was neither inevitable nor everlasting, and with wise action we can make the world better. For this reason, anti-colonial campaigns retell the story of empire, and African Americans remember the cruelty of the slave trade. Their purpose is not to cling to the past but to free themselves from it.

units.name: 128 Self-Esteem
units.passage: Throughout most of Western history, children were regarded as naturally wicked creatures who required firm control, and adults commonly relied on physical punishment and intimidation to make them behave. The notion that young people are emotionally delicate is, in fact, a fairly recent invention. Nowadays, countless parents are frozen by the worry that they might leave a lasting emotional wound on their children, believing that one wrong move could cause pain for the rest of a child's life. This anxious urge to protect kids from any psychological unease does not stop at the front door. Many elementary schools, for instance, hand out weekly "star student" prizes to every single pupil, regardless of effort or achievement. To some extent, bringing the insights of developmental psychology and a spirit of empathy into child-rearing and schooling marks genuine progress, since it allows children to feel valued and to grow intellectually in a secure atmosphere. Still, we have gone too far. By making childhood excessively sterile, we lock children inside a cushioned room where they can never get hurt but also never learn to prepare for real life. When we puff up their self-esteem with empty compliments and spare them the natural results of their choices, we breed impatience, a sense of entitlement, and blindness to their own weaknesses, and then send them out into a world that will not soften their landings.

units.name: 129 The Daily Record
units.passage: The news industry might fairly be described as a machine for producing novelty, because it fixes its attention on incidents, shocks, and breaks in the ordinary flow of life. A sudden act of violence or an unexpected crash in stock prices will claim far more airtime than a long-standing problem that slowly damages a society year after year. As Thomas E. Patterson, a Harvard scholar who studies government and the press, observes, the most serious troubles a society faces seldom lead the headlines for exactly this reason. Each new story abruptly pushes yesterday's aside, so that every morning seems to begin a brand-new world. In this setting, freshness is valued above all, and so is certainty. A report needs a concrete event to feel urgent, while matters of public policy develop gradually across months or years. As a result, the news turns into a never-ending series of crises, creating a confused and fragmented picture in which the pressing moment wins out over careful, long-term reflection. Many people assume that following the news helps them understand the wider world, yet research has shown that in almost no case did the reported events match the actual course of developments. Drowned in a flood of urgent "right now" stories, the larger pattern disappears; the media resembles a broken-up record of events rather than a faithful mirror of society.

Little did she know what was waiting for her.
Rarely he goes out on weekends.
Not until midnight she finished her homework.
Hardly the train had left when it began to rain.
items.exp: 부정어구가 문두에 오면 '조동사+주어+동사' 순서로 도치돼요. Little did she know만 올바르고, 나머지는 도치가 되지 않았어요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How Harvard Scholars Study the Press
The Rise of Stock Market Reporting
Why Violence Dominates Our Cities
News as a Novelty Machine: Losing the Big Picture
Breaking News: The Fastest Way to Understand Society
items.exp: The news industry might fairly be described as a machine for producing novelty라고 시작해, 긴급한 사건에 묻혀 the larger pattern disappears라고 끝나는 글이에요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: The news becomes an endless series of crises in which the urgent present crowds out long-term reflection.
A sudden stock market crash receives less attention than a slowly developing social problem.
Yesterday's stories are revisited daily so that readers see continuity.
The author believes the media offers a faithful mirror of society.
News reports can feel urgent without being tied to any concrete event.
items.exp: the news turns into a never-ending series of crises, creating a confused and fragmented picture in which the pressing moment wins out over careful, long-term reflection이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Because the news favors (A) ___ events over slowly unfolding issues, it offers a (B) ___ picture of society instead of a coherent one.
choices: (A) sudden — (B) complete
(A) sudden — (B) scattered
(A) gradual — (B) scattered
(A) sudden — (B) balanced
(A) political — (B) scattered
items.exp: 뉴스는 incidents, shocks, and breaks in the ordinary flow of life에 주목하고 그 결과 a broken-up record of events가 된다고 했어요. 갑작스러운(sudden) 사건을 좇아 조각난(scattered) 그림을 만든다는 요약이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [every morning seems to begin a brand-new world]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Each new story abruptly pushes yesterday's aside, so that every morning seems to begin a brand-new world.)
choices: newspapers are redesigned every morning to attract readers
society genuinely changes so fast that yesterday is irrelevant
journalists wake up early to be the first to report
the media celebrates optimism about the future each day
the news presents each day's events without connecting them to what came before
items.exp: Each new story abruptly pushes yesterday's aside라고 했어요. 어제의 이야기를 밀어내고 날마다 새 사건만 다루니 전날과의 연결이 끊긴다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: a machine for producing [novelty]
will claim far [more] airtime than a long-standing problem
the most serious troubles a society faces [frequently] lead the headlines
A report needs a [concrete] event to feel urgent
the larger pattern [disappears]
items.exp: 원문은 seldom lead the headlines예요. 뉴스가 돌발 사건에 집중하기 때문에 사회의 가장 심각한 문제들이 헤드라인에 거의 오르지 못한다는 맥락이므로 frequently는 반대 뜻이에요.

units.name: 130 Problem Solving Techniques
units.passage: Recognizing that we belong to something larger than ourselves allows us to take a break. We can regain our strength after hard effort, confident that others, who have also looked after their own well-being, are ready to carry the work forward. This idea matters not only for personal health; it is equally vital when we confront wide-reaching social problems such as climate change. If people believe that global warming can be handled only through individual effort, they easily fall into defeatism. Naturally, no single person can fix the crisis alone. For this reason, it pays to take stock, from time to time, of all the commitment and skill that exist around us, a practice sometimes called asset or capacity mapping, and to collect accounts of people who have succeeded, so that we are surrounded by reminders of what groups have accomplished together. Doing this helps us remember that personal actions add up to a broader social effect, one that grows steadily over the years. Building strong community networks seems far more achievable than persuading every person on Earth to cut emissions or to stop the oceans from rising. In other words, we do not have to carry the whole weight ourselves; what we can do is play our part and trust others to play theirs.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 거대한 사회 문제는 집단적 노력으로 해결할 수 있으며, 이를 인식하면 무력감에서 벗어날 수 있다.
기후 변화는 개인이 탄소 배출을 줄이는 것만으로 해결된다.
공동체를 유지하려면 개인이 휴식 없이 희생해야 한다.
실패 사례를 분석하는 것이 성공 사례를 모으는 것보다 중요하다.
사회 문제 해결의 책임은 전적으로 정부에 있다.
items.exp: 혼자 해결할 수 없는 기후 변화 같은 문제도 집단의 성과를 떠올리면 패배주의를 벗어나 해결 가능하다고 느낀다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 글쓴이는 휴식이 집단의 성과를 떨어뜨린다고 본다.
기후 변화를 개인 차원에서만 해결할 수 있다고 믿으면 의욕이 커진다.
자산 지도화(asset mapping)는 개인의 실패 원인을 찾는 활동이다.
개인의 행동은 시간이 지나면서 더 큰 사회적 영향으로 쌓인다.
전 세계 사람의 배출량을 줄이는 것이 공동체 네트워크를 만드는 것보다 쉽다.
items.exp: 'personal actions add up to a broader social effect, one that grows steadily over the years'라고 했어요.

items.q: 글쓴이가 주변의 참여와 재능을 점검하고 성공 사례를 모으라고 권하는 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 다른 사람들과 성과를 경쟁하기 위해
집단이 함께 이룬 성과를 상기하여 패배주의를 이겨 내기 위해
개인의 책임을 다른 사람에게 떠넘기기 위해
기후 변화의 심각성을 과장하기 위해
성공한 사람들의 방식을 그대로 모방하기 위해
items.exp: 패배주의를 언급한 뒤 'For this reason'으로 이어지며, 집단의 성과를 떠올리게 하는 것(reminders of what groups have accomplished together)이 목적이라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 'defeatism'의 영영 풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: a strong desire to win at any cost
the practice of sharing work with others
an attitude of expecting failure and giving up easily
the belief that the environment must be protected
a feeling of pride in a group's success
items.exp: 혼자서는 해결할 수 없다고 느껴 생기는 태도이므로 실패를 예상하고 쉽게 포기하는 태도예요.

items.q: 다음 문장에서 [밑줄 친 동사]가 단수형인 이유로 가장 적절한 것은? Recognizing that we belong to something larger than ourselves [allows] us to take a break.
choices: ourselves가 문장의 주어이기 때문에
something이 단수 대명사이기 때문에
that절이 복수 명사를 수식하기 때문에
현재완료 시제로 쓰였기 때문에
동명사구(Recognizing ~ ourselves)가 주어이기 때문에
items.exp: 주어는 동명사구 Recognizing that ~ ourselves이고, 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 allows가 쓰였어요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: You Don't Have to Carry It All: Trusting the Collective
Climate Change: A Problem Only You Can Solve
The Importance of Rest for Personal Health
Mapping Community Assets: A Technical Guide
Why Individual Efforts Never Matter
items.exp: we do not have to carry the whole weight ourselves; what we can do is play our part and trust others to play theirs가 결론이에요. 개인 행동도 사회적 효과로 쌓인다고 했으므로 Never Matter는 맞지 않아요.

items.q: According to the passage, what allows us to take a break after hard effort?
choices: The knowledge that the crisis has already been solved.
A belief that individual effort alone can handle global warming.
The confidence that others who have cared for themselves are ready to carry the work forward.
The realization that our actions have no real effect.
An official schedule that assigns rest periods to each person.
items.exp: We can regain our strength after hard effort, confident that others, who have also looked after their own well-being, are ready to carry the work forward라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Seeing ourselves as part of a larger (A) ___ effort protects us from (B) ___ when facing problems too big for any individual.
choices: (A) collective — (B) responsibility
(A) individual — (B) despair
(A) scientific — (B) laziness
(A) collective — (B) success
(A) collective — (B) despair
items.exp: Recognizing that we belong to something larger than ourselves라고 했고, 개인 노력만으로 해결하려 하면 they easily fall into defeatism이라고 했어요. 집단적(collective) 노력에 속한다고 보면 패배감(despair)을 피할 수 있다는 요약이에요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (In other words, we do not have to carry the whole weight ourselves; what we can do is ___.)
choices: persuade every person on Earth to cut emissions
play our part and trust others to play theirs
take on more responsibility than anyone else
wait until experts solve the crisis for us
record our own achievements for future generations
items.exp: no single person can fix the crisis alone이라며 주변의 commitment and skill을 믿으라고 했어요. 각자 제 몫을 하고 다른 사람도 그럴 것이라 믿는다는 결론이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: who have also [looked] after their own well-being
when we [confront] wide-reaching social problems
they easily [fall] into defeatism
Building strong community networks [seem] far more achievable
one that [grows] steadily over the years
items.exp: 주어는 동명사구 Building strong community networks이므로 단수 동사 seems가 맞아요. 바로 앞의 복수 명사 networks에 맞추면 틀려요.

units.name: 131 Theories of Art
units.passage: Classical painting is full of food. Take a well-known canvas by Nathaniel Bacon, in which a kitchen maid holds a gigantic melon surrounded by huge cabbages and ripe peaches. This lavish display honors plenty, yet it hides the hard work of growing, cooking, and eating what is shown. Strangely, however, images of people actually eating are rare, a remarkable gap if we think of art as a means of representing life. Even Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper, a painting about a meal, shows no one in the middle of a bite. Today's social media feeds are likewise packed with carefully styled pictures of dishes, but we seldom glimpse the less attractive sight of jaws chewing. I suspect that human vanity plays a role in this odd pattern. Eating is a physical process that is by nature awkward and messy: we drool, gnaw, and swallow. However much we wish to keep up an image of ourselves as perfect beings, eating gives us away; to eat is to confess that we share in the disorder of the natural world. That may explain why artists and image-makers have avoided showing it: it forces us to face the undeniable fact that we have bodily needs. Faced with that fact, the mirror simply chooses not to reflect.

items.q: 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Joy of Sharing Meals Online
How Classical Painters Celebrated Abundance
Hidden Bites: Why Art Avoids Showing Us Eating
The Health Benefits of Fruits and Vegetables
The Secret Symbols of The Last Supper
items.exp: 음식은 많이 그려지지만 먹는 장면은 드물고, 그 이유가 완벽해 보이고 싶은 인간의 허영심 때문이라는 글이에요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Bacon의 그림은 음식을 수확하고 요리하는 노동을 자세히 보여 준다.
다빈치의 「최후의 만찬」에는 음식을 베어 먹는 사람이 그려져 있지 않다.
소셜 미디어에는 음식 사진이 거의 올라오지 않는다.
글쓴이는 먹는 행위가 본래 우아하다고 본다.
고전 회화에는 음식이 거의 등장하지 않는다.
items.exp: 'Even Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper ... shows no one in the middle of a bite'라고 했어요.

items.q: 글쓴이가 먹는 장면이 잘 묘사되지 않는 이유로 추측하는 것은?
choices: 음식 재료가 너무 비쌌기 때문에
화가들에게 먹는 모습을 그리는 기술이 부족했기 때문에
종교적으로 먹는 장면을 그리는 것이 금지되었기 때문에
완벽한 존재로 보이고 싶은 인간의 허영심 때문에
소셜 미디어의 게시 규정 때문에
items.exp: 'I suspect that human vanity plays a role'라고 하고, 완벽한 존재라는 이미지를 지키고 싶어 한다고 설명해요.

items.q: 문맥상 지문의 'gives us away'의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: protects us
satisfies us
ignores us
delights us
reveals our true nature
items.exp: 완벽해 보이고 싶어도 먹는 행위가 우리가 자연의 무질서에 속한다는 사실을 '드러낸다'는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은? [However much] we wish to keep up an image of ourselves as perfect beings, eating gives us away.
choices: [However hard] he tried, he couldn't open the door.
[However], the plan failed in the end.
[How] did you solve the problem so quickly?
I don't know [how much] this jacket costs.
She asked me [how often] I exercise.
items.exp: '아무리 ~해도'라는 양보의 복합관계부사 however예요. However hard he tried도 같은 쓰임이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the symbolism of melons and peaches in Baroque painting
how social media changed the way we photograph meals
why images of eating are absent from art despite its abundance of food
the physical mechanics of chewing and swallowing
the hidden labor behind lavish food displays
items.exp: Classical painting is full of food이지만 images of people actually eating are rare하다는 역설을 제시하고, 그 이유를 human vanity로 설명하는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, why is the rarity of eating scenes called 'a remarkable gap'?
choices: Art is supposed to represent life, yet it leaves out something everyone does.
Painters of the past lacked models willing to be shown eating.
Food was too valuable to be shown being consumed.
Religious rules forbade depicting meals in progress.
Social media has only recently made food fashionable.
items.exp: a remarkable gap if we think of art as a means of representing life라고 했어요. 삶을 재현하는 예술이 모두가 하는 먹는 행위를 빼놓았기 때문에 눈에 띄는 공백이라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Art and social media eagerly display food but avoid showing people eating, because the act exposes our (A) ___ nature, which conflicts with our desire to appear (B) ___.
choices: (A) bodily — (B) hungry
(A) social — (B) flawless
(A) spiritual — (B) humble
(A) bodily — (B) flawless
(A) bodily — (B) generous
items.exp: 먹는 행위는 the undeniable fact that we have bodily needs를 직면하게 하고, 이는 an image of ourselves as perfect beings를 지키려는 바람과 충돌한다고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [the mirror simply chooses not to reflect]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Faced with that fact, the mirror simply chooses not to reflect.)
choices: people avoid looking at themselves while eating
mirrors were rarely included in classical paintings
artists lack the technical skill to paint reflections
viewers refuse to see the hidden labor behind food
art, which should show life, deliberately leaves out our bodily nature
items.exp: 앞에서 예술을 a means of representing life, 즉 삶을 비추는 거울로 보았어요. 그 거울이 we have bodily needs라는 사실을 비추지 않기로 한다는 것은 예술이 먹는 모습을 의도적으로 외면한다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: images of people actually eating are [rare]
This lavish display [conceals] plenty
packed with carefully [styled] pictures of dishes
a physical process that is by nature awkward and [messy]
the [undeniable] fact that we have bodily needs
items.exp: 원문은 This lavish display honors plenty예요. 거대한 멜론과 양배추, 복숭아가 풍요를 '기리는' 것이고, 뒤의 yet it hides와 대조되어야 하므로 conceals는 맞지 않아요.

units.name: 132 What Is Information Platform?
units.passage: A one-time global public policy chief working for a major technology firm once declared that, as a provider of geographic reference material, the company ought to remain neutral in territorial conflicts between nations. The firm insists that its maps reflect "ground truth," meaning the physical and social landscape that someone standing at the spot would actually see. For instance, it marks contested borders in Crimea with a dashed line, and the map a person sees differs depending on where that person is located. Yet the very fact that these regional versions exist seriously weakens the claim that the firm offers one objective "ground truth." In reality, what it calls factual is ultimately determined by the company's own institutional choices. Businesses frequently exaggerate the virtues of what they sell, boasting of the "best coffee in the world" or "three times the shine," but this appeal to "ground truth" may be more serious than ordinary advertising hype. The content of the firm's maps and mapping system can clash with the sovereignty of nations as defined by international law. Furthermore, because the platform is used almost everywhere, the company has acquired a kind of authority over legal and territorial disputes that no one ever formally gave it.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 디지털 지도는 국제 분쟁을 해결하는 가장 객관적인 도구이다.
기술 기업은 사용자 위치에 따라 지도를 더 다양하게 만들어야 한다.
기업의 과대광고는 소비자에게 아무런 해가 되지 않는다.
지도 기업의 '지상 실측 정보'는 중립적이지 않으며, 기업이 부여받지 않은 권위를 영토 분쟁에서 행사하고 있다.
국제법은 디지털 지도 기업의 결정을 따라야 한다.
items.exp: 지역별 버전의 존재가 객관성 주장을 약화하고, 사실이라는 것도 회사의 결정으로 정해지며, 공식적으로 받지 않은 권위를 얻었다고 비판해요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 그 기업은 크림반도의 분쟁 국경을 실선으로 표시한다.
모든 사용자는 위치와 상관없이 동일한 지도를 본다.
글쓴이는 지역별 지도 버전이 기업의 객관성을 강화한다고 본다.
그 기업은 국제기구로부터 영토 분쟁에 관한 공식 권한을 위임받았다.
기업 지도의 내용은 국제법상 국가 주권과 충돌할 수 있다.
items.exp: 'The content of the firm's maps ... can clash with the sovereignty of nations as defined by international law'라고 했어요.

items.q: 윗글에서 'best coffee in the world'와 'three times the shine'을 언급한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 흔한 상품 과대광고의 예를 들어 '지상 실측 정보' 주장이 그보다 더 심각할 수 있음을 대비하기 위해
커피 산업이 지도 산업보다 규모가 크다는 것을 보여 주기 위해

units.name: 133 Conversational Maxims
units.passage: In everyday talk, much of what we say is unplanned, especially when we are meeting new contacts at an event or being asked to answer a question on the spot. Many people find such moments stressful because they assume there exists one ideal way of speaking that they must somehow discover. We feel obliged to offer a grand insight, something profound, elegant, or even transcendent, as though each remark had to be as ambitious as a cathedral rising over a city. This expectation tends to backfire. The effort to say exactly the right thing clutters our thoughts, makes our delivery stiff and nervous, and keeps us from noticing how our listeners are reacting or letting our own character come through. What we overlook is that supplying the humble brick, the basic unit from which conversations are built, is just as valuable, and perhaps more so. We lay that groundwork by pausing, paying close attention, and occasionally pointing out how the ideas others have raised relate to one another. The conversational maxims, the principles that guide effective exchanges, do not demand that every comment be novel or revolutionary; often, the most meaningful role a speaker can play is to sustain the dialogue and link its scattered parts. Good communication, then, is less about erecting monuments than about setting down bricks, one considered contribution after another.

units.name: 134 Language Beyond Words
units.passage: Progress in machine learning is welcome, yet the philosophy of language offers reasons to doubt that Artificial Intelligence will ever capture what makes the human mind distinctive. Early in his career, Ludwig Wittgenstein, together with Bertrand Russell, among the towering thinkers of the twentieth century, held that language could be broken down into its "atomic" elements, much as AI systems try to do now. If the hidden logical form of a statement were laid bare, they reasoned, one could determine whether it was true or false. This approach, known as logical positivism, was celebrated as the end of philosophy, since its supporters believed that philosophical puzzles were merely confusions about terms, which could be studied, clarified, and settled. After the First World War, however, Wittgenstein turned against his own earlier view more fiercely than anyone, insisting that language has no deep logical skeleton, because a word means whatever its use makes it mean. No word, on this account, carries a fixed literal or original sense; meaning is something people share, and it lives only within context. Human intelligence, unlike its artificial counterpart, is thus a social phenomenon. The real worth of AI technology, then, lies in highlighting and strengthening what is unique about the human mind, helping us make full use of it and support one another.

units.name: 135 Game On!
units.passage: Whatever we label or treat as sport seems to require an other: individuals or teams set against you, each of whom might win and therefore stands as a rival for the title you are pursuing. If this is so, how should we think about non-competitive sports in which only a single person takes part? One answer is that such activities are built around an inner rivalry. Imagine someone who remembers her fastest time on a familiar bike route and sets out to improve on it. Her effort mirrors a cycling time trial, in which riders compete one by one over an identical course, starting at intervals rather than together. What she aims to overcome here is not another rider but a former version of herself. In a similar way, countless runners now rely on GPS-enabled apps that map their routes and store their personal records. Sport, it seems, can still be understood through the idea of othering. The athlete treats her present self as the genuine self, while her past selves, along with their best results, are cast as opponents to be surpassed. Such cases indicate that the spirit of conventional sport survives even when the competition is directed entirely at oneself.

units.name: 136 Analog vs. Digital
units.passage: To many doubters, the arrival of digital recording was nothing short of scandalous. Older machines had vibrated in sympathy with the sounds they captured, whereas the new technology sliced those vibrations into bits that were encoded and later reassembled on a compact disc. Purists complained that the result was a sort of android music; one compared hearing a CD to viewing the world through a window screen, with something always standing between the listener and the sound. Such worries, however, tend to be offset by other developments. Recording technology has helped unknown performers build careers and given support to those who had no foothold in the industry. Nowhere is this clearer than in the history of African American music. Almost from the start, recordings allowed people living on the margins of the culture to make themselves heard, armed with little more than a guitar and their own voices. Records opened up a global stage that would otherwise have remained closed to them. Indeed, they played a vital part in advancing the civil rights of African Americans, and this fact places the long-running argument over whether technology has truly benefited music in its proper perspective.

units.name: 137 Social Biases
units.passage: Because dogs can pick up sounds at high frequencies, trainers have long relied on whistles that dogs can hear but humans cannot, so that the animals can be commanded without disturbing anyone nearby. At some point, the idea of the dog whistle found its way into politics. A familiar case is the habit of calling Barack Obama by his complete name, "Barack Hussein Obama." At first glance, nothing seems wrong with this, since that is, after all, what he is called. Ordinarily, however, we leave out middle names unless the person in question uses them, and had his middle name been John or Walker, nobody would have bothered to spell it out. Hussein, though, is a name found most often among Muslims. The purpose of stressing it is to associate Obama with Islam and, through that association, with damaging stereotypes about extremism and terrorism. Dog whistles of this kind are ethically slippery, since they come with plausible deniability built in: the speaker can always claim innocence. Still, there is reason for hope. If we can be persuaded that they are tied to underlying bias and concealed intentions, such messages can be pulled into the range everyone can hear, where they can be openly rejected.

items.exp: 개 호루라기는 특정 집단만 듣는 소리라는 비유이므로, '모두가 들을 수 있는 범위로 끌어온다'는 것은 숨은 의도를 공개적으로 드러내 모두가 알아보게 한다는 뜻이에요. 뒤에 openly rejected가 이어져요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: whistles [that] dogs can hear but humans cannot
nothing [seems] wrong with this
a name [found] most often among Muslims
the speaker can always [claim] innocence
so that the animals can [command] without disturbing anyone
items.exp: 동물들은 명령을 '받는' 대상이므로 수동태 can be commanded가 되어야 해요. 원문은 so that the animals can be commanded without disturbing anyone nearby예요.

units.name: 138 Are Choices Free?
units.passage: The choice-centered view, which places individual decisions at the heart of its analysis, has real strengths, yet it overlooks the systemic nature of markets. An arrangement that offers people a variety of options can nonetheless exercise a kind of social control over how they live. This happens when the arrangement structures the available options so that a broader social pattern is preserved, much as the streets of a city govern the way its residents travel. Motorists are free to pick whichever route they like, but the design of the roads and the timing of the traffic lights channel their movements into larger patterns, such as recurring congestion at certain points. In much the same way, market prices reshape the sets of options people face, pulling everyone into particular patterns of producing and consuming. Consider the housing market. Many residents with modest incomes find that they can no longer pay to live in the city center and are gradually pushed toward the edges, while the affluent cluster in the central districts. The outcome is socio-economic segregation, a pattern that seems to emerge from personal choice, from what people decide as shoppers, employees, or investors, but that is in fact molded by the market arrangement itself.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 개인의 선택은 시장 구조와 무관하게 완전히 자유롭다.
도시의 도로망을 개선하면 교통 체증을 없앨 수 있다.
개인의 자유로운 선택처럼 보이는 결과도 시장 구조가 만든 사회적 통제의 산물일 수 있다.
저소득층은 스스로 원해서 도심 외곽을 선택한다.
선택 중심 관점은 아무런 장점이 없는 이론이다.
items.exp: 선택지를 주는 체제도 사회적 통제를 할 수 있으며, 개인 선택처럼 보이는 계층 분리가 실제로는 시장 구조에 의해 만들어진다고 주장했어요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 선택 중심 관점은 시장의 체계적 성격을 잘 설명한다.
다양한 선택지를 제공하는 체제는 사회적 통제를 할 수 없다.
운전자들은 도로 설계 때문에 경로를 전혀 선택할 수 없다.
부유층은 주로 도시 외곽 지역에 모여 산다.
시장 가격은 사람들이 마주하는 선택지의 범위를 바꾼다.
items.exp: market prices reshape the sets of options people face라고 했어요. 부유층은 중심 지역(central districts)에 모여 살아요.

items.q: 윗글에서 도시의 도로망 예시가 보여 주는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 개인이 자유롭게 선택해도 구조가 전체적인 흐름의 패턴을 만들어 낸다.
교통 신호는 운전자의 안전을 위해 존재한다.
도로가 많을수록 교통 체증이 줄어든다.
운전자들은 항상 가장 짧은 경로를 선택한다.
도시 계획은 주택 시장과 아무런 관련이 없다.
items.exp: 운전자는 경로를 자유롭게 고르지만 도로 설계와 신호 시간이 움직임을 정체 같은 더 큰 패턴으로 이끈다고 했어요.

items.q: 윗글의 affluent의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: poor
wealthy
elderly
ambitious
local
items.exp: 소득이 적은 주민(residents with modest incomes)과 대조되어 중심부에 모여 사는 사람들이므로 wealthy(부유한)의 뜻이에요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
The outcome is socio-economic segregation, a pattern [that] seems to emerge from personal choice.
choices: It is true [that] he lied to us.
She was so tired [that] she fell asleep.
The fact [that] she won surprised us.
He has a car [that] runs on electricity.
I think [that] he is right.
items.exp: that은 a pattern을 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사예요. a car를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사 that과 같아요. 나머지는 접속사 that이에요.

items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Best Routes Through City Traffic
Why Rich People Prefer the City Center
The Complete Strengths of the Choice-Centered View
Free to Choose, Yet Steered: How Markets Shape Our Lives
Ending Housing Shortages Through Better Planning
items.exp: 선택지가 많아도 시장 구조가 사람들을 particular patterns of producing and consuming으로 끌어들여 사회적 통제를 한다는 내용이므로, 자유롭게 선택하지만 조종된다는 제목이 알맞아요. 도로와 주택은 예시일 뿐이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, why do many residents with modest incomes move toward the edges of the city?
choices: Because the city builds better roads near the edges.
Because they can no longer afford to live in the city center.
Because they prefer quieter neighborhoods.

Because the affluent pay them to leave.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Even when a market offers many (A) ___, the way it structures them steers people into collective patterns, so outcomes that look freely chosen are in fact (B) ___ by the system.
choices: (A) options — (B) shaped
(A) options — (B) ignored
(A) restrictions — (B) shaped
(A) prices — (B) rejected
(A) options — (B) reversed

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (An arrangement that offers people a variety of options can nonetheless exercise a kind of ___ over how they live.)
choices: personal freedom
economic growth
social control
moral judgment
random influence

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: it [overlooks] the systemic nature of markets
a broader social pattern is [preserved]
[channel] their movements into larger patterns
are gradually [pushed] toward the edges
is in fact [untouched] by the market arrangement itself
items.exp: 계층 분리는 개인 선택에서 나온 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 시장 구조가 '만들어 낸(molded)' 것이라는 게 글의 결론이에요. untouched(영향을 받지 않은)는 정반대의 뜻이에요.

units.name: 139 Linear vs. Nonlinear
units.passage: When we judge quality, our thinking needs an additional instrument: the idea that the best and the worst are separate yet equally important. Rather than sitting at two ends of one continuous line, the highest and lowest qualities of a product are frequently independent of each other. History offers cases where this perspective could have warned evaluators about grave consequences no one intended. Take asbestos as an example. When this material was being developed, its makers ranked insulation along a single line. Top-quality insulation was simply whatever met certain design targets, such as keeping heat in and blocking out noise. Poor insulation, by contrast, was given no features of its own; it was merely any material that fell short of those targets set in advance. As a result, while marketing insulation for homes, nobody foresaw the much graver problems that emerged in practice. Asbestos, valued for resisting heat and lasting for decades, turned out to be poisonous, and foam insulation, being an ideal place to build nests, could draw in destructive rodents. If the makers had examined the lowest qualities on their own terms, without linking them to the highest ones, they might have been far better able to imagine dangers that had nothing to do with the product's intended purpose.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 제품의 최고 품질을 높이는 것이 위험을 줄이는 가장 확실한 방법이다.
품질의 최상과 최악을 별개의 차원으로 평가해야 예상치 못한 위험을 내다볼 수 있다.
단열재는 소음 차단보다 열 보존 기능을 우선해야 한다.
제품 평가는 소비자의 선호도를 기준으로 이루어져야 한다.
설계 목표를 엄격하게 정할수록 제품의 품질은 향상된다.
items.exp: 최고와 최악은 하나의 선 양 끝이 아니라 서로 독립적이며, 최악을 따로 검토했다면 의도와 무관한 위험을 상상할 수 있었을 거라는 게 글의 요지예요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 석면 제조업자들은 품질을 여러 개의 독립된 기준으로 평가했다.
최악의 단열재는 고유한 위험 특성으로 정의되었다.
석면은 열에 약하다는 단점 때문에 비판받았다.
단열 폼은 둥지를 틀기 좋아 설치류를 끌어들일 수 있었다.
주택용 단열재를 판매할 당시 석면의 독성은 이미 널리 알려져 있었다.

items.q: 석면 제조업자들이 정한 '최고의 단열재'의 기준으로 글에 언급된 것은?
choices: 열 보존과 소음 차단이라는 설계 목표의 달성
저렴한 생산 비용
설치의 편리함
인체에 대한 무해성
설치류를 막는 효과
items.exp: Top-quality insulation was simply whatever met certain design targets, such as keeping heat in and blocking out noise라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 poisonous와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: durable
invisible
flexible
expensive
toxic
items.exp: poisonous는 '독성이 있는'이라는 뜻으로 toxic과 같아요. 열에 강하고 오래가지만 결국 해롭다는 문맥이에요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]을 같은 의미로 바꿔 쓸 때 어법상 알맞은 것은? '[If the makers had examined] the lowest qualities on their own terms, ..., they might have been far better able to imagine dangers ...'
choices: Did the makers examine
Have the makers examined
Had the makers examined
Were the makers examined
The makers had examined if

items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Asbestos: The Perfect Insulation Material
How to Set Clear Design Targets
Rodents and the Problem of Foam Insulation
A Brief History of Home Building
Best and Worst Are Not Two Ends of One Line

items.q: According to the passage, what might the makers have been better able to do if they had examined the lowest qualities on their own terms?
choices: Lower the production cost of insulation.
Improve heat retention even further.
Imagine dangers unrelated to the product's intended purpose.
Market the product to more homes.
Prove the product completely safe.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Because the makers judged insulation on a (A) ___ scale, poor insulation was defined merely as a failure to meet targets, so dangers (B) ___ to those targets went unforeseen.
choices: (A) single — (B) unrelated
(A) single — (B) essential
(A) double — (B) unrelated
(A) flexible — (B) central
(A) single — (B) identical

items.q: 밑줄 친 [given no features of its own]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Poor insulation, by contrast, was given no features of its own; it was merely any material that fell short of those targets set in advance.)
choices: it was a material with no physical properties at all
it was defined only as the absence of good qualities, not examined for its own distinct risks
it was never actually sold on the market
it had exactly the same features as top-quality insulation
its makers refused to describe it to buyers
items.exp: 뒤에서 it was merely any material that fell short of those targets라고 풀어 주었어요. 나쁜 단열재를 그 자체의 특성(독성, 해충 유인 등)으로 보지 않고 단지 '목표 미달'로만 규정했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: cases where this perspective could have [warned] evaluators
such as [keeping] heat in and blocking out noise
those targets [set] in advance
valued for resisting heat and [to last] for decades
foam insulation, [being] an ideal place to build nests
items.exp: 전치사 for의 목적어로 resisting과 and로 병렬되므로 동명사 lasting이 와야 해요. 원문은 valued for resisting heat and lasting for decades예요.

units.name: 140 Urban Planning
units.passage: Seattle residents who noticed new bicycle racks beneath a bridge mostly took them to be an innocent piece of public infrastructure. A few observers, however, pointed out that the spot was strangely remote and hardly convenient for anyone actually riding a bike. Looking into the matter, they found that city officials had placed the racks there to remove places where homeless people might set up camp, while hiding what the racks were really for. Hidden intentions of this kind expose the politics built into the spaces we share. Armrests on benches, which stop people from stretching out, are harder to criticize, since one can argue they serve a practical function in certain situations, regardless of whether that function is the real reason they exist. Other features, though, are especially misleading obstacles whose concealed purpose is kept from the public. Whether we approve of them or not, such hostile designs restrict what people are able to do in public, and they often drive vulnerable groups into areas that are less visible and more hazardous. However admirable the stated goals of some designs may appear, they rest on a risky way of thinking about public space: they treat the symptoms instead of the underlying causes, and they simply move social tensions elsewhere rather than resolving them.

items.q: 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 공공시설 설계 속에 숨겨진 배제의 의도를 비판적으로 살펴야 한다.
자전거 이용자를 위해 공공 거치대를 늘려야 한다.
벤치의 팔걸이는 노약자를 위해 반드시 설치해야 한다.
노숙인 문제는 도시 외곽으로 이전하여 해결해야 한다.
공공 디자인은 미적 가치를 최우선으로 고려해야 한다.
items.exp: 숨은 의도를 가진 방어적 디자인이 취약 계층을 밀어내고 근본 원인은 해결하지 못한다며 그 논리를 비판하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 대부분의 주민은 다리 아래 자전거 거치대를 무해한 시설로 여겼다.
일부 관찰자는 거치대의 위치가 자전거 이용자에게 불편하다고 지적했다.
시 당국은 거치대의 설치 목적을 시민들에게 공개적으로 밝혔다.
벤치 팔걸이는 특정 상황에서 실용적이라는 주장이 가능하다.
방어적 디자인은 취약 계층을 더 위험한 곳으로 밀어낼 수 있다.
items.exp: 당국은 노숙인 야영을 막으려고 설치하면서 진짜 용도를 숨겼다(while hiding what the racks were really for)고 했어요.

items.q: 필자가 일부 디자인의 사고방식을 위험하다고 보는 이유로 글에 언급된 것은?
choices: 건설 비용이 지나치게 많이 들기 때문에
자전거 이용률을 떨어뜨리기 때문에
도시 미관을 해치기 때문에
법적 분쟁을 일으키기 때문에
근본 원인 대신 증상만 다루고 갈등을 다른 곳으로 옮기기 때문에
items.exp: they treat the symptoms instead of the underlying causes, and they simply move social tensions elsewhere라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 remote의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: operated from a distance
far from where people usually go
only slightly possible
emotionally cold
very modern
items.exp: 자전거 이용자에게도 불편할 만큼 '외진' 장소라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 [ ]에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? 'Other features, though, are especially misleading obstacles [ ] concealed purpose is kept from the public.'
choices: which
that
what
whose
whom
items.exp: 뒤에 관사 없는 명사 concealed purpose가 오고 '그 장애물의 숨겨진 목적'이라는 소유 관계이므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose가 와요.

items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Seattle's Growing Need for Bicycle Racks
Hostile Design: The Hidden Politics of Public Space
Why Every Bench Needs Armrests
A Guide to Modern Urban Architecture
How Cities Finally Solved Homelessness
items.exp: Hidden intentions of this kind expose the politics built into the spaces we share라며 숨은 목적을 가진 적대적 디자인을 비판하는 글이므로, 공공 공간의 숨은 정치를 담은 제목이 알맞아요. 자전거 거치대는 도입 예시일 뿐이에요.

items.q: What does the author say about the stated goals of some hostile designs?
choices: They are always openly shared with the public.
They have successfully resolved social tensions.
They focus on underlying causes rather than symptoms.
However admirable they may appear, they rest on a risky way of thinking about public space.
They make public space more accessible to vulnerable groups.

units.name: 141 Everyday Exposure
units.passage: Content confusion arises when marketing is disguised so well that readers can no longer tell solid information apart from a gentle attempt to sell them something. Online outlets, for example, run pieces such as "Seven Habits for a More Energetic Start to Your Day." On the surface these seem to offer helpful tips for daily living, yet they quietly present a particular coffee brand as something no morning should be without. Many readers take this sponsored material for honest guidance, which shows how thoroughly ads can merge with ordinary content until audiences fail to notice that someone is selling to them. If this trend were followed to its logical end, we would arrive at a world without any genuine content at all, in which every piece of writing is a sales pitch of one kind or another. Such an extreme is admittedly improbable, but advertising is already slipping smoothly into material that looks noncommercial, flooding the media landscape and shoving actual journalism to the edges. The explanation is straightforward. When profit is the aim, serious content inevitably gives way to clickbait, quizzes, and amusing videos of cats, all of which keep us online longer in the hope that we will eventually buy something.

units.name: 142 Beyond Competition
units.passage: Aesthetic experience is not confined to galleries; it pervades every corner of human life, which is why the philosopher John Dewey described art as a form of experience. Sport, too, carries considerable aesthetic worth, giving shape to ideals of physical perfection and to a pursuit of excellence passed down from the ancient Greeks and from those who established the Olympic Games. The histories of art and sport are closely intertwined. Since classical antiquity, a wide variety of works have shown how the two are linked, with beauty, form, and excellence plainly on display. Boxing offers a striking case. Though frequently regarded as a savage entertainment, it can, surprisingly, produce moments of remarkable beauty. George Bellows, an American realist painter of the early twentieth century admired for his energetic and expressive brushwork, depicted both the grace and the roughness of prizefighting in Stag at Sharkey's. In this painting, the boxers' tense muscles, contorted bodies, and exposed moments suggest more than a physical contest; they convey the profound human drama of endurance, fear, and pride. As Bellows's canvas vividly shows, sport, even in its fiercest forms, possesses an expressive force that speaks to our sense of beauty.

units.name: 143 A Challenge for All
units.passage: It is commonly believed that government ought to keep its distance from moral and religious controversies, because mixing the two tends to breed coercion and intolerance. Many people suppose that honoring the moral and religious beliefs of fellow citizens requires setting those beliefs aside and running public affairs as if they did not exist. Yet such an approach does not truly sidestep disagreement; it merely pushes it underground, and this suppression may in turn spark resentment and a hostile reaction. Consider the bans on the hijab adopted in several European nations. Because open debate was largely absent, the measures provoked fiercer resistance and left the communities concerned feeling targeted. By contrast, engaging more vigorously and publicly with our moral differences could lay a firmer foundation for mutual respect. A historical illustration is provided by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa. Rather than muting complaints about earlier abuses of human rights, it confronted them in the open, encouraging conversation and helping the nation heal. Instead of steering clear of the values our citizens hold, then, we should engage with them more directly, at times questioning and disputing them, and at times hearing them out and learning from them.

units.name: 144 Intellectual Property
units.passage: The question of who authors a work produced by AI has become such a tangled knot that the wisest answer may be to treat AI's first output as belonging to the public domain, much like an object someone finds lying on the street. Put differently, rather than trying to unravel this authorship puzzle, we might simply sever the bond of ownership altogether and leave the work free for everyone to use. Debating ownership in this case, after all, resembles chasing a leash that has no dog attached to it. Several reasons support this view. First, placing such works in the public domain sidesteps immediate conflicts with the existing system of intellectual property, and it matches the position already taken in numerous countries, where AI-generated works cannot be copyrighted. Second, the theory behind intellectual property law holds that it exists to safeguard human creativity alone; where exclusive rights are not clearly needed to encourage creation, tradition suggests they should be granted to no one. Third, a machine cannot itself assert copyright, since only human beings may make such claims. Because nobody holds a valid claim over creations that are not human, these works naturally fall into the public domain.

units.name: 145 Understanding Achievement
units.passage: Picture a remarkably gifted student who has always worked hard, earns outstanding grades, and is admitted to an elite university that nearly every applicant dreams of attending. Once she arrives on campus, however, she discovers that her classmates are every bit as talented and committed as she is, and a number of them have accomplished even more. If she keeps defining herself mainly by her grades and her intelligence, as she has done for years, she may find it hard to settle into this fiercely competitive setting. What she needs first is a kind and patient attitude toward her own struggles, viewing herself gently as a small fish that has unexpectedly been placed in a much larger and tougher pond. Feeling overwhelmed at first is natural, and she should allow herself time to adjust. Next, while she works to match the pace of the remarkable peers around her, she will require considerable emotional agility, which lets her see her identity in wider and more flexible terms rather than through test scores alone. After that, she must move along with the flow of change and accept her new reality. Should she fail to revise the way she perceives herself, she may end up as a stagnant fish trapped in a pond that has grown too large for her.

units.name: 146 Concept, Conceptualization
units.passage: Concepts are not passive tools; they actually shape the methods we use to reason, much as influential people and powerful institutions do. We build our conceptualizations ourselves, and at first glance they seem to exist merely to satisfy our passing whims by helping us make sense of the world. Yet they achieve this by organizing, screening, and adjusting the way we experience reality, along with the way we think and feel about it. Concepts guide where our attention goes, direct the flow of our emotions, steer our imagination, and arrange our memories. Beyond that, they rule over our reasoning itself: they set certain patterns of thought in motion and quietly inform us about what is important, which reasons deserve to be called good, and what conclusions we ought to draw. Because their influence is so pervasive, concepts shape how we live and how we relate to other people, and they even frame the accounts we give of our own actions and experiences. For this reason, the way we view and apply concepts can never be neutral. Consider freedom. Many people treat it simply as personal choice and overlook other interpretations, such as freedom as something produced through shared responsibility. Recognizing the power of concepts and examining them critically is therefore essential if we want to think and act independently.

units.name: 147 Paradox of Plenty
units.passage: At times, if we hope to grasp what is really going on around us, we must take a step back and observe events from an unfamiliar angle. That is the essence of “standing apart”: remaining in your place while viewing the world as though you were a stranger to it. Standing apart provides a much-needed pause, letting us keep faith in a fairer world even as we live within the present one. This faith undermines the myths and superstitions that the media often keeps alive, including racism, xenophobia, and various other fears. In the current attention economy, social media, advertisers, and news outlets all compete for our attention purely to make money, and as a result they lock us inside an anxious, fearful present. Since these forces work to shrink our view, our job is to nurture an imagination that remains untainted by the disappointment their stories spread. Above all, though, standing apart does not mean running away. It means choosing to remain, to live in a different way, and to join others who likewise refuse to accept things as they are. Such resistance is a matter of engaging on your own terms, even when some people label it wrong because it questions the existing system. Yet it is exactly this challenge that creates fresh ways of thinking and living.

units.name: 148 Nonverbal Communication
units.passage: As digital communication keeps developing, I have become more and more attracted to voice messages as a substitute for exchanges based on text. Written messages lack what voice notes naturally contain: paralinguistic features such as tone, pace, and inflection, which carry emotional subtleties that text tends to flatten. This extra layer of expression builds a stronger feeling of connection and immediacy between the person speaking and the person listening. Yet what really won me over was the incidental context those recordings captured. Sounds in the background, like children at play, the clatter of pots and utensils in a kitchen, or a soft laugh after a story about someone's first date, are not distractions at all. Instead, they add richness to the message and make the speaker feel present. Hearing them gave me the sense that we were sharing the same space, yet it never required me to reply right away. In a time marked by digital overload and emotional distance, that quality mattered enormously. It was through experiences like these that I started recording voice notes myself, perhaps hoping to offer someone else the same closeness I had felt.

units.name: 149 Consumer Characteristics
units.passage: In the business world, there is little doubt that performance standards will keep climbing, and more relentlessly than ever before, which makes truly excellent performance all the more valuable. The chief cause is that information technology has handed customers a degree of power never seen before, and armed with it, they expect more. Anyone who has bought something online knows this from experience. As individual shoppers, we now have access to far more information than was ever available in the past. We can, for instance, discover what a car dealer actually paid for a vehicle, and we know that a textbook priced at $135 at the campus bookstore can be bought online for about $70. Yet the knowledge and savings of ordinary consumers are tiny compared with what corporate purchasers have learned about their suppliers, along with the cost reductions they can extract from those suppliers by exploiting that knowledge. The strategy consultant Gary Hamel puts the point sharply: if your profits depend on customers not knowing things, you are in trouble. Companies that once relied on an information advantage can no longer count on it, because informed buyers will simply go elsewhere.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Because information technology has made customers far more (A) ___, companies can no longer profit from buyers' ignorance and must deliver (B) ___ performance.
choices: (A) knowledgeable — (B) average
(A) loyal — (B) superior
(A) patient — (B) faster
(A) knowledgeable — (B) cheaper
(A) knowledgeable — (B) superior
items.exp: we now have access to far more information than was ever available이라 했고, 그래서 truly excellent performance all the more valuable해진다고 했어요. 그래서 (A) knowledgeable, (B) superior가 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [informed buyers will simply go elsewhere]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Companies that once relied on an information advantage can no longer count on it, because informed buyers will simply go elsewhere.)
choices: customers will move to live in another country
customers who know the facts will switch to competitors offering better value
customers will stop shopping altogether
customers will become suppliers themselves
customers will only search the internet instead of buying
items.exp: 교과서를 서점 대신 온라인에서 약 70달러에 사는 것처럼, 가격을 아는 구매자는 더 나은 조건을 주는 다른 판매자로 옮겨 간다는 뜻이에요. 그래서 if your profits depend on customers not knowing things, you are in trouble이라고 했어요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: which [makes] truly excellent performance all the more valuable
far more information than [was] ever available in the past
what a car dealer actually [paid] for a vehicle
Anyone who has bought something online [know] this from experience
the cost reductions they can [extract] from those suppliers
items.exp: 주어 Anyone은 단수이므로 관계절 who has bought ~ 뒤의 본동사도 knows가 되어야 해요. 원문은 Anyone who has bought something online knows this from experience예요.

units.name: 150 The Logic of Relationships
units.passage: In today's complicated world, being just requires more than holding abstract values and beliefs; it also calls for a careful grasp of how causes produce effects. Suppose you spent the day gathering mushrooms so your children could eat, and someone seized the basket from you by force. All your effort would be wasted, and your children would go to bed hungry. Clearly, this is unfair and unjust, and anyone can see it, because both where the harm began and what it led to are plain. Sadly, however, our global society is by nature so branched and interconnected that we easily lose track of which actions lead to which consequences. We may stay quietly at home without ever lifting a finger against anyone, yet activists point out that our comfortable lifestyle rests on children working in miserable sweatshops in poorer countries. Animal-welfare advocates likewise remind us that our daily lives are linked to billions of farm animals kept in the harshest conditions ever known. Does the fact that you personally do nothing wrong give you the right to feel righteous? In my view, it does not. Justice now demands that we trace the hidden chains connecting our comfort to the suffering of others.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 개인이 직접 잘못하지 않았다면 도덕적 책임은 없다.
동물 복지보다 아동 노동 문제를 먼저 해결해야 한다.
현대 사회에서 정의를 실천하려면 원인과 결과의 관계를 철저히 이해해야 한다.
정의는 추상적인 가치와 신념만으로 충분히 실현된다.
사회 운동가들의 주장은 과장되어 있으므로 경계해야 한다.
items.exp: 첫 문장과 마지막 문장에서 정의는 인과 관계를 꼼꼼히 파악하고 숨은 연결 고리를 추적할 것을 요구한다고 주장해요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 버섯 바구니 예시에서는 피해의 원인과 결과를 파악하기 어렵다.
현대 세계는 매우 얽혀 있어 인과 관계를 놓치기 쉽다.
운동가들은 편안한 삶이 아동 노동에 기반한다고 지적한다.
동물 복지 옹호자들은 우리 삶이 농장 동물과 연결되어 있다고 말한다.
글쓴이는 직접 잘못하지 않았다는 이유로 정당하다고 느끼는 것에 반대한다.
items.exp: 버섯 예시는 피해의 시작과 결과가 'plain'(분명)해서 누구나 부당함을 알 수 있다고 했어요.

items.q: 윗글에서 버섯 바구니 사례를 누구나 쉽게 부당하다고 판단하는 이유는?
choices: 피해자가 어린아이들이기 때문
버섯이 값비싼 식량이기 때문
법으로 금지된 행위이기 때문
가해자가 자신의 잘못을 인정했기 때문
피해가 어디서 시작되어 무엇으로 이어졌는지 분명하기 때문
items.exp: 'because both where the harm began and what it led to are plain'에서 이유를 밝히고 있어요.

items.q: 윗글의 righteous의 영영 풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: deeply ashamed
legally guilty
physically comfortable
morally right or justified
openly angry
items.exp: 직접 잘못하지 않았다는 이유로 스스로를 '도덕적으로 옳다'고 느낄 자격이 있느냐고 묻는 문맥이에요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
Sadly, however, our global society is by nature so branched and interconnected [that] we easily lose track of which actions lead to which consequences.
choices: I think [that] he is right.
She spoke so softly [that] no one could hear her.
It is clear [that] she told a lie.
The car [that] he bought is red.
It was yesterday [that] I met him.
items.exp: 지문은 'so ~ that ...'(너무 ~해서 …하다) 결과 구문이에요. 'so softly that ~'도 같은 구문이에요.

items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Simple Ethics of Mushroom Gathering
Tracing the Hidden Chains: Justice in an Interconnected World
Why Activists Exaggerate Global Problems
Farm Animals and the Future of Food
How to Avoid Ever Doing Wrong
items.exp: Justice now demands that we trace the hidden chains connecting our comfort to the suffering of others라는 결론처럼, 얽힌 세계에서 숨은 인과 고리를 추적해야 정의롭다는 글이에요. 버섯과 농장 동물은 예시예요.

items.q: In the mushroom example, why would the children go to bed hungry?
choices: Because the mushrooms turned out to be poisonous.
Because the parent forgot to cook them.
Because the forest had run out of mushrooms.
Because someone took the basket away from the parent by force.
Because the children refused to eat them.
items.exp: someone seized the basket from you by force. All your effort would be wasted, and your children would go to bed hungry라고 했어요. 버섯이 독이 있다거나 숲에 없었다는 내용은 없어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In a simple case the link between a harm and its cause is (A) ___, but in our interconnected world such links are hidden, so justice requires us to (B) ___ how our comfort depends on others' suffering.
choices: (A) obvious — (B) uncover
(A) obvious — (B) ignore
(A) obscure — (B) uncover
(A) obvious — (B) deny
(A) invisible — (B) forget
items.exp: 버섯 예시는 where the harm began and what it led to are plain이라 했고, 현대 사회에서는 trace the hidden chains해야 한다고 했어요. 그래서 (A) obvious, (B) uncover예요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [without ever lifting a finger against anyone]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (We may stay quietly at home without ever lifting a finger against anyone, yet activists point out that our comfortable lifestyle rests on children working in miserable sweatshops in poorer countries.)
choices: without using our hands to do any work
without pointing at anyone in public
without taking any direct harmful action toward others
without voting against any candidate
without touching anyone else's belongings
items.exp: lift a finger against는 '~에게 손가락 하나 대다, 해를 가하다'라는 뜻이라, 직접 누구를 해치지 않는다는 의미예요. 그런데도 우리 삶이 아동 노동과 연결되어 있다는 yet 뒤의 대비와 맞아요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: being just requires more than holding [abstract] values
so [branched] and interconnected that we easily lose track
farm animals kept in the [harshest] conditions ever known
trace the [hidden] chains connecting our comfort
All your effort would be [rewarded]
items.exp: 바구니를 강제로 빼앗겼으니 하루의 노력은 '허사가 된(wasted)' 것이고, 그래서 아이들이 굶는다는 흐름이에요. rewarded(보상받은)는 정반대 뜻이에요.
